mistakes.note: Sefa, a raider chief left standing all night with her crossbow on her arm by a captain who had handed his pistol away, lets him take the crossbow and rope her in half a sentence while her riders ride off; the dawn answer she demanded from the courier is never asked.
The caravan is two days out of Port Lell, yet the border post it passed on the way lies three days back.
Vane orders Sefa to stand away from the woman, though she had left Tamsin and stood at the water skins by Jory; the lantern set on the gravel now swings on a hook.
Five riders were counted on the dunes and at their camp; with Sefa held in the hollow, five more ride to the herd and five sets of tracks leave at dawn.
Vane, who rode a horse from the border post, sits a camel from here to Ashar.
Vane counts seven people in a caravan of five, and eighteen skins now serve a caravan whose tally Jory gave as a hundred and forty.
Told only to sit by the skins and watch the haze, Wren is walked along the rim to find and follow the riders' tracks.
Sefa's crossbow, slung on Vane's saddle, is recorded as carried by Wren, and round 34 offers a Choice with my crossbow across my knees.
The Choice picked asks Vane what a soldier of his was doing with grey cloth in his pocket, though Wren watched Vane pocket it himself, and he has to correct her.
Jory is recorded as knowing what Tamsin told Wren of Sefa, which no one told him, and it is kept in his summary.
Tamsin and Sefa are recorded as hearing Wren refuse the offer in front of Tamsin, when Wren held her tongue and stayed back in the dark.

The Ossery thread's now and plans hold the letter thread's events (Sefa's haggle, Vane's pistol, the riders at the herd) through round 21 and again at 33, and the riders' plans to close on the caravan by 14:00 and 15:00 lapse with nothing on the page.
Two Loose Ends the page left behind (how many skins to drink at the Red Teeth, what Wren will tell Vane of Sefa's offer) stay open to the end, while the slit skin found at M68 opens none.
Wren wears her straw hat again on the ridge, but the record keeps it carried, and later pictures show her bareheaded on the Flats at noon.
His burn scar down the neck is drawn as a fresh cut down the face, in both portraits.
The redrawn Sefa is a pale, shaved-headed woman where the first portrait showed brown skin and dark hair under the hood; the page never says her head is shaved.
Vane aims the pistol at Wren muzzle first, where the page has him offer it butt first.
Tamsin stands on foot with both hands whole, where the page has her mounted and two fingers short, and the wall of dust is drawn as a mud wall.

choices.reason: Three real paths most rounds and picks bend what follows (the empty satchel returns as a Choice at round 21), but rounds 17 and 39 offer near-twins and two Choices misread the page.

surprise.reason: The riders at the herd while Sefa is held, Vane's search of the saddle and the blue-coat who paid for the riders' water all land from what was set up, though the dusk visit was told in full beforehand.

threads.reason: The letter thread bends to every refusal, but on day 3 the riders' planned strikes lapse twice off the page, and the Free Wells and Ossery threads barely reach it.

characters.reason: Tamsin, Vane and Jory hold their voices and wants, but Sefa turns from a menace into a docile captive at M72 with no cause shown.

continuity.reason: No scene breaks, but a careful reader catches a run of slips: Vane's horse become a camel, seven people of five, 140 skins become eighteen, a sixth rider, the opening's days.

pacing.reason: The night at the Red Teeth holds, but the saddle talk circles for five replies, the day's ride teases a rider and a storm that both deflate, and Sefa's capture is settled in a clause.

prose.reason: Vivid, concrete and in one voice, with tics (unhurried, the ruined hand, the crust rang) and a few garbled lines, the rewrite's own words in Tamsin's mouth at M19 among them.

pictures.reason: Scenes mostly show the moment with the right people and dress, but Vane's scar is on the wrong place, Sefa changes skin and hair, and M34 shows the pistol aimed at Wren.

secrets.reason: Marrick, the demand, Ossery's knife and Jory's guilt all stay hidden; Vane's suspicion comes out by his own act, and Ossery's lead is won on a Check.

agency.reason: Moves are carried out as given and the pistol is left for the player to take; only M70 walks Wren off to track the riders unasked.

stakes.reason: Eight Checks on risky moves, and failures carry (the riders know her from the ridge, the saddle stays ruined), but the successes at M19 and M56 win little.

state.reason: Journal, lore, time and scene stay true, but a crossbow enters Wren's things and a Choice, two people know what they never heard, and two Loose Ends go stale.

adventure.reason: The Red Teeth, the crust and the well are each their own place and the raiders close in twice, but danger stays a standoff: no blow lands in 45 rounds, and the day's threats thin away before they arrive.
